# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-30 (Extended v204)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to summer Year 8. Primary Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Sewer des Halles, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry, Quay, Passy, Pont de Jéna, Bercy, Amelot sewer, Isle Louviers, Quartier Popincourt, Ménilmontant, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery, Arsenal, Faubourg Saint-Honoré, Quartier Saint-Georges, Quartier des Martyrs, gallery des Martyrs, Beautreillis sewer, Quai des Ormes, Grève, Place du Châtelet, Pont Notre-Dame, Quai de la Mégisserie. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny, Jondrette's garret, Montfermeil.

Paris sewer system: 5,300 fathoms (1663); 40,300 metres (1 January 1832); follows 2,200 streets; ridge divides waters to Seine or Grand Sewer; Sainte-Avoye sewer marks watershed culmination. Grand Sewer (old brook of Ménilmontant) terminates blind sack at foot of Ménilmontant knoll. **Fontis phenomenon** (dangerous water-saturated ground): depth 3-4 to 8-10+ feet; discard loads to escape; death slow if earth predominates, prompt if water. **Champs-Élysées quagmire**: 1836 Faubourg Saint-Honoré sewer reconstruction took six months. **Sewer outlet design flaw**: pointed arch vault narrows funnel-like; heavy grating at river outlet, double-locked with rust-caked lock, rarely swung hinges, iron staple sunk deep. Key exists (held by Thénardier). Beyond: open air, daylight, shore (Grand-Caillou—solitary point), distant quays, bridge of Jéna (downstream), bridge of Invalides (upstream).

**Seine rapid at Châtelet**: Between Pont Notre-Dame and Pont au Change; between Quai de la Mégisserie and Quai aux Fleurs. Water hurries formidably through arches in vast terrible waves; attacks bridge piles with liquid ropes. Men falling in never reappear.

**Summer Year 8 seasonal conditions**: Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Light went early. Rain threatened but held off. Recent rains swollen river. Darkness complete after midnight; ceiling of clouds concealed stars. Not a single light burned in houses; no one passing; all streets and quays deserted. Notre-Dame and towers of Court-House seemed features of night. Street lantern reddened margin of quay. Bridges lay shapeless in mist. Wind came off water with salt and tar smell. Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps.

## English Subplot Summary

**Rumored claims**: Yera Stenworth confided fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided same. In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures forged. Kassa Brackick whispered Islan Thornmere secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge rumored Rorald Lindmere dead of plague.

**Confirmed rumors**: Fire at Dunstead granary set on purpose. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood.

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate lodgings. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work, moved there (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate lodgings (autumn Year 7). Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married only son of Luena Stenenridge at Ostcombe; couple lived there thereafter. Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there thereafter. Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7). Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month. Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven. Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford. Islan Thornmere died of old age, quietly in sleep at Dungate. Gadrek Prydenridge married eldest daughter of Lura Haskick in chapel at Ostcombe; couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. Luvie Prydenridge and Semor wed at Ostcombe. **Luena Stenenridge sent copper chalice by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it safely.** In letter Gadrek burned, revealed old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar. Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair roof of chapel at Kelmere, and shook on it. **Havie Prydenridge never did keep promise made to Gadrek Prydenridge (pay old debt owed to Stenworth family); matter abandoned.**

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7).

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work never begun.

**Property**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it. **Kassa Brackick gave amber map to Volan Stenworth (summer Year 8).**

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade. **Barricade combat (6th June)**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Marius's wound (6th June)**: Shot broke collar bone; felt fainting and falling. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Marius's medical condition and recovery (Chapters 27-30)**: Bullet deadened by pocket-book, turned aside, made tour of ribs with hideous laceration, not dangerous. Long underground journey dislocated broken collar-bone seriously. Arms slashed with sabre cuts. Head fairly covered with cuts. Grave symptom: swoons caused by wounds; might cause brain damage. Exhausted by hemorrhage.

**Recovery**: 7 September, four months after being brought back (dying condition), doctor declared Marius would recover. Convalescence began. Forced to remain two months more on long chair due to collar-bone fracture. One last wound type will not close, prolongs dressings indefinitely. This long illness saved him from all pursuit—six months extinguishes even public wrath. Gisquet order outraged public opinion and King; wounded protected; councils of war did not dare trouble any one. Marius left in peace.

**M. Gillenormand's devotion**: Passed through all manner of anguish, then every form of ecstasy. Had big armchair carried to Marius' bedside; required daughter to take finest linen for compresses. Gillenormand would not permit explanation that batiste not good as coarse linen, nor new as old linen. Present at all wound dressings. When dead flesh cut away, said: "Aïe! aïe!" Offered cooling-draught to wounded man. Overwhelmed doctor with questions, repeated same ones. At each improvement phase, grandfather raved. Executed multitude of mechanical actions full of joy; ascended and descended stairs without knowing why. Sent big bouquet to pretty female neighbor. Tried to draw Nicolette upon knees. Called Marius "M. le Baron." Shouted: "Long live the Republic!" Gazed upon Marius with eyes of grandmother. Brooded over him while he ate. No longer knew himself, no longer rendered himself account. Marius was master of house; abdication in grandfather's joy. In state of joy, grandfather was most venerable of children. Stepped behind to smile lest he might fatigue. Content, joyous, delighted, charming, young. White locks added gentle majesty to gay radiance. Grace mingled with wrinkles is adorable; indescribable aurora in beaming old age.

**Marius's wariness**: Not won over, little softened by grandfather's solicitude and tenderness. Not in the secret; in reveries of invalid, possibly still feverish, distrusted tenderness as strange and novel thing for conquest. Remained cold. Marius said to himself all right so long as he did not speak and let things take course; but when question of Cosette arose, grandfather's true attitude would be unmasked. Unpleasant scene would follow: recrudescence of family questions, confrontation of positions, sarcasm, objections, Fauchelevent, Coupelevent, fortune, poverty, stone about his neck, future. Violent resistance; conclusion: refusal. Marius stiffened himself in advance.

## Javert's Moral Crisis and Death (Chapter 30)

**Change in consciousness**: Up to day of Valjean's emergence, Javert borrowed from Napoleon only resolution and certainty. Now whole person slow and sombre, stamped with anxiety. For several hours, Javert ceased to be simple, was troubled; brain so limpid in blindness lost transparency; crystal clouded. Duty divided within conscience.

**Encounter at Seine**: When unexpectedly encountered Valjean on banks of Seine, beheld two paths, both equally straight, both contrary. Which was true?

**Valjean's transformation in Javert's perception**: Valjean disconcerted him. All axioms crumbled. Valjean's generosity crushed him. Facts formerly treated as lies recurred as realities. M. Madeleine reappeared behind Jean Valjean; two figures superposed, forming one venerable image. Something terrible penetrated soul—admiration for convict. Respect for galley-slave—possible? Shuddered, could not escape. Confess sublimity of wretch. Odious.

**Moral transformation perceived**: Benevolent malefactor, merciful, gentle, helpful, clement, convict returning good for evil, giving pardon for hatred, preferring pity to vengeance, preferring to ruin himself rather than ruin enemy. Kneeling on heights of virtue, more nearly akin to angel than man. Javert constrained to admit monster existed.

**Loss of certainty**: Supreme anguish was loss of certainty. Felt uprooted. Code no longer anything but stump in hand. Had to deal with scruples of unknown species. Sentimental revelation entirely distinct from legal affirmation, his only standard hitherto. Whole order of unexpected facts cropped up, subjugated him. New world dawning: kindness accepted and repaid, devotion, mercy, indulgence, violences by pity on austerity, respect for persons, no more definitive condemnation, possibility of tear in eye of law, no one knows what justice according to God, running inverse to justice according to men. Perceived terrible rising of unknown moral sun; horrified and dazzled. Owl forced to gaze of eagle.

**Superior authority consciousness and rift**: This new chief, God, became unexpectedly conscious of; felt embarrassed by him. Unforeseen presence threw off bearings. Up to this point, everything above merely smooth, limpid, simple surface; nothing incomprehensible. Authority was plane surface; no fall in it. Suddenly terrified by unprecedented apparition: gulf on high. Could not return Valjean to Rue de l'Homme Armé. It was clear that was what ought to do. Could not.

**Suicide (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Traversed Place du Châtelet diagonally, regained quay, returned to very point abandoned quarter hour previously. Darkness complete, sepulchral moment following midnight. Ceiling of clouds concealed stars. Not single light burned in houses; no one passing; streets and quays deserted. Street lantern reddened margin of quay. Bridges lay shapeless in mist. River could not be seen; only foam audible. In dizzy depth, gleam of light appeared, undulated vaguely. Wall abrupt, mingled with vapors, produced effect of escarpment of infinite. Fierce breath rose from abyss. Flood divined rather than perceived, tragic whispering of waves, melancholy vastness of arches of bridge, imaginable fall into gloomy void—all shadow full of horror. Remained motionless several minutes, gazing at opening of shadow. Water roared. Took off hat, placed it on edge of quay. A moment later, tall black figure appeared erect upon parapet, bent over towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down into shadows; dull splash followed; shadow alone in secret of convulsions of obscure form disappeared beneath water. **Javert is dead (suicide by drowning).**

## Other Events (Chapter 30)

**Boulatruelle**: Escaped neatly from Jondrette's garret with other ruffians; drunkenness was salvation. Authorities never made out whether he was robber or robbed. Nolle prosequi set him at liberty. Returned to road from Gagny to Lagny, making broken stone under administrative supervision. One morning before daybreak, caught sight through branches of man whose back alone he saw; shape of shoulders not entirely unfamiliar. Man did not belong in countryside, just arrived, on foot evidently, no public conveyance passes through Montfermeil at that hour. Had walked all night. From Paris, no doubt. Compassed hundred strides before day broke. Footprints stamped in sand, weeds trodden down, heather crushed, young branches in brushwood bent and in act of straightening pointed out track. Followed it, then lost it. Time flying. Plunged deeper into woods, came to eminence. Early huntsman whistling air of Guillery suggested climbing tree. Old but agile. Beech-tree of great size stood close at hand. Boulatruelle ascended beech as high as able. Man entered open glade at considerable distance, masked by large trees, but glade Boulatruelle knew from noticing near large pile of porous stones an ailing chestnut-tree bandaged with sheet of zinc nailed directly upon bark. This glade formerly called Blaru-bottom. Heap of stones visible thirty years ago doubtless still there. By beaten paths required quarter hour; in bee-line through underbrush, dense, thorny, aggressive, full half hour necessary. Boulatruelle committed error of not comprehending this, believed in straight line. Thicket struck him as best road. Man made better time than expected; Boulatruelle's pursuit difficult.

**Minor English figures**: Luvie fell asleep in chair before fire had caught. Ilrald bought ribbon at stall and then regretted it. Yera Haskick only shrugged when Havie asked "Will it rain, do you think?" Luvie Prydenridge asked same question of Yera Haskick; she only shrugged.
